analysis_status: robustness stress test motivated by the homogeneous-detection assumption in the simple two-season model; not a new confirmatory ecology analysis
purpose: Test whether latent gain/loss inference is robust to extra-binomial heterogeneity in per-census interaction detection.
scope: same six strict_dated_core_2008_2010 transitions and same focal-response-excluded candidate dyad surface

models.binomial_detection: parent two-season model with transition-specific constant p_previous and p_current
models.beta_binomial_detection: same latent state process, but detections conditional on z=1 follow beta-binomial distributions with transition-specific mean p_previous/p_current and concentration kappa_previous/kappa_current

diagnostics.aic_preference: beta-binomial is materially preferred when AIC is at least 2 below the binomial model within a transition
diagnostics.state_boundary: record whether gamma or epsilon is at |logit| >= 7.9; boundary estimates are evidence against stable latent-transition identification under the richer observation model
diagnostics.cross_transition_stress: report counts of transitions with beta-binomial AIC preference and state-boundary estimates; do not convert these counts into an independent p-value

interpretation.allowed: assess whether the simple detection-corrected latent transition estimates are sensitive to plausible overdispersion in repeated census detections
forbidden: claiming beta-binomial detection is the true observation process
using a richer model to rescue a preferred ecological conclusion

claim_ceiling: If beta-binomial detection materially outperforms the simple binomial model and destabilizes gamma/epsilon estimates, the correct conclusion is model-sensitive latent rewiring, not detection-corrected ecological rewiring. This stress test cannot identify the true observation process.
